sections.description: This section outlines the patient’s baseline clinical status, comorbidities, and the sequence of events leading to the first transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). It frames the clinical problem that necessitated eventual repeat interventions, highlighting the importance of context in decision‑making.
subtopics: Patient demographics, comorbidities and risk scores (EuroSCORE II, STS‑PROM)
History of aortic valve disease and initial 2014 Lotus TAVI: indications and procedural details
Early postoperative course and first valve performance (ejection fraction, gradients, valve area)
Clinical decline in 2021: symptom progression, echocardiographic findings, and the decision to re‑intervene
Pre‑procedure assessment for TAV‑in‑TAV: imaging modalities, hemodynamic thresholds, and risk stratification

sections.section_title: 2. TAV‑in‑TAV and the Development of Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
sections.description: This section examines the second TAVI procedure, the complications that emerged, and the subsequent episode of infective prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE). It discusses how infection altered valve biomechanics and the ensuing therapeutic strategy.
subtopics: Details of the 2022 Evolut TAV‑in‑TAV implantation (access, sizing, and procedural complications)
Post‑operative ventricular remodeling and echocardiographic response
Presentation of PVE: clinical features, microbiology (Enterococcus faecalis), and diagnostic work‑up (TEE, MSCT, blood cultures)
Antimicrobial therapy regimen, duration, and criteria for infection resolution
Impact of PVE on valve leaflet integrity, structural degeneration, and decisions on further reintervention

sections.section_title: 3. Pre‑procedural Imaging and Strategy Development for TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV
sections.description: Focused on the pivotal role of multimodal imaging, this section explains how CT‑guided planning informed valve choice, implantation depth, commissural alignment, and coronary protection strategies for the third intervention.
subtopics: Multislice CT parameters: annular sizing, valve‑to‑coronary distances, sinus dimensions, and ostial heights
Assessment of overlapping valve frames and expected neo‑skirt geometry
Integration of 3‑D modeling and fluoroscopic landmarks for commissural alignment
Choice of the Acurate neo2 (self‑expanding, supra‑annular) based on frame height, hemodyamics, and coronary clearance
Pre‑implantation planning: balloon pre‑dilation, rapid pacing strategy, and high‑implantation targets
Contingency planning for coronary obstruction and haemodynamic failure

sections.section_title: 4. Technical Execution and Immediate Post‑procedure Assessment
sections.description: Detailing the intervention itself, this section describes the procedural workflow, valve deployment technique, and how outcomes were verified according to VARC‑3 criteria.
subtopics: Access strategy (left radial + femoral), hemodynamic monitoring, and anesthesia considerations
Guidewire navigation, balloon pre‑dilation, and aortography for coronary patency
Valve positioning, alignment with the Evolut leaflets, and stair‑stepped implantation
Post‑dilation technique and radial expansion dynamics
Immediate post‑procedural imaging: angiography, TEE confirmation of valve function and residual regurgitation
VARC‑3 endpoint evaluation: hemodynamics, device success, and complications

sections.description: This section presents the short‑ and long‑term clinical course after the third TAVI, highlighting improvements, persistent challenges (e.g., patient‑prosthesis mismatch), and surveillance protocols.
subtopics: Early post‑procedure TTE findings: gradient, AVA, indexed AVA, DVI, and remodeling
One‑month and 3‑month echocardiographic trends, symptom status, and functional classification
One‑year follow‑up: hemodynamics, EF, absence of PPM progression, and clinical stability
Management of residual PPM: low‑gradient behavior, therapeutic options, and impact on prognosis
Long‑term surveillance plan: imaging frequency, infection monitoring, and potential future interventions
Analysis of procedural durability and comparison with existing literature on serial TAVI

sections.section_title: 6. Clinical Lessons, Future Directions, and Ethical Considerations
sections.description: The final section synthesizes learning points, discusses the evolution of treatment paradigms for multiple TAVI reinterventions, and reflects on multidisciplinary decision‑making, patient autonomy, and emergent technologies.
subtopics: Key take‑aways: imaging‑driven planning, commissural alignment, and coronary protection in triple‑stented anatomy
Implications for lifetime valve management: early strategy discussion, choice of valve design, and surgical vs. transcatheter routes
Emerging solutions for future failure: valve fracture, BASILICA, leaflet laceration, and their applicability to complex anatomies
Ethical and shared decision‑making: informed consent, risk communication, and off‑label device use
Guideline alignment: ESC 2025 recommendations for PVE and repeated TAVI, and where this case aligns or deviates
Future research needs: registries, registrational trials, and computational modeling for prediction of outcomes in serial TAVI
